title: Imperial Dynasty Envoys
next_chapter_hook: At the moment Chen Ji's fingertips were about to touch that forbidden secret manual, the Tianji Record suddenly shuddered, as if issuing some kind of warning—the price of this transaction was far heavier than he had imagined.

text.content:
In the Tianqing Sect Council Hall, the setting sun dyed the sky blood-red.

Chen Ji stood with hands clasped behind his back in the shadows of the hall corner, his expression calm as always, only his fingertips gently stroking the fragmented Tianji Record hidden in his sleeve. The previous negotiation with Su Qingyao had drained most of his mental energy, but just as he was about to leave quietly—in that instant, the spiritual energy throughout the entire hall suddenly froze.

It was as if an invisible giant hand had gripped the throat of heaven and earth, even the air solidifying into amber. That oppressive pressure did not come from any cultivator, but from something far more ancient and transcendent, like a deity gazing down at ants.

The hall doors silently opened.

A figure in black imperial robes strode in, the five-clawed nine dragons embroidered in gold and silver threads flowing with otherworldly magnificence under the setting sun. The visitor did not deliberately release any aura, yet every step fell upon the hearts of all living beings.

Chen Ji's pupils constricted.

He had seen old monsters at the Transformation God Stage, witnessed the护法 elders of the Demonic Holy Sect, and even glimpsed the residual shadows of ancient fierce beasts at the edge of forbidden grounds—but never had any existence given him such pure pressure.

It was a force that transcended all cultivation systems, the embodiment of ten thousand years of faith condensed into mortal imperial power.

dialogue.content:
The black-robed figure stopped in the center of the hall, not looking at anyone present, yet his gaze seemed to penetrate层层虚空, landing directly on Chen Ji.

"The keeper of the Tianji Record..."

The voice was not loud, yet it erupted like a great bell in Chen Ji's Mental Sea.

"This envoy has been waiting for you for a long time, Chen Ji."

text.content:
Chen Ji's heart trembled violently, but his expression remained unchanged.

He slowly stepped out from the shadows, bowed respectfully, his posture impeccable: "I was unaware of your arrival, Your Excellency. I have failed to welcome you properly. But I wonder... how did Your Excellency learn my name?"

His voice was steady, but his spine had drawn taut as a bowstring.

He had suppressed the Tianji Record's aura to the extreme, yet the other party still identified him with a single phrase—what did this mean? Did it mean the Imperial intelligence network had penetrated every corner of the cultivation world, or... was there a insider?

dialogue.content:
The black-robed figure's lips curved slightly, a half-smile playing at the corners.

"Cang Yutian unified the mortal world ten thousand years ago, establishing the system of Chess Players, walking the world with the will of Heavenly Dao. This envoy is the blood descendant of that Chess Player—the legitimate successor of Great Zhou, a Wanderer of the Yutian Pavilion, Ji Wujiu."

He raised his hand, and a golden token suspended above his palm, inscribed with the characters "御天" in archaic and primitive style, emanating an ancient aura identical to that of the Tianji Record.

"This token was forged by Cang Yutian from Heavenly Dao's source before his fall. Summoning you here specifically—you should understand what this means."

text.content:
Chen Ji lowered his gaze, his thoughts racing like lightning.

Cang Yutian. Chess Players. Heavenly Dao Source.

Each word weighed like mountains, each piece of information tearing new fissures in his original understanding. None of these secrets were recorded in the Tianji Record Fragment, and Mo Xiansheng had never mentioned them—

No, perhaps they had never truly been unmentioned.

Chen Ji suddenly recalled Mo Xiansheng's profound words: "The origin of the Tianji Record is far more ancient than you imagine. And its shackles... are far more inescapable than anything you could break free from."

Could it be that the Tianji Record was not merely an inheritance artifact, but—

dialogue.content:
"It seems you have already guessed a few things."

Ji Wujiu stood with hands clasped behind his back, his gaze down at Chen Ji carrying a hint of amusement.

"The Tianji Record is not some ancient fortuitous encounter, but an insurance policy laid down by Cang Yutian—using prophets as chess pieces to peer into Heavenly Secrets and correct fate's calculations. And each generation of keepers has been nothing more than a puppet dancing on the strings of Heavenly Dao's will."

He paused, his voice turning cold: "You think you're scheming to control the world? Hmph... From the moment you accepted the Tianji Record, you became the most pitiful piece on the chessboard."

text.content:
Chen Ji slowly straightened, the reverence gone from his face, replaced by a hint of cold indifference.

"Your Excellency speaks truly."

His voice was平静得近乎冷酷: "Since I am merely a chess piece, may I ask Your Excellency—what does one chess piece warrant such elaborate summoning?"

In his sleeve, the Tianji Record Fragment faintly radiated heat.

Chen Ji sensed some kind of summons welling up from deep within the Tianji Record, resonating with the token in Ji Wujiu's palm. That was... the aura of Heavenly Dao's source, sharing the same roots as his incomplete Tianji Record.

choice.prompt: Ji Wujiu's appearance completely disrupted Chen Ji's calculations. In this unknown chess game, he must decide his next strategy—

choices.description: Directly question Ji Wujiu's true intentions to probe his cards and bottom line
choices.visible_cost: Reveal part of your own hidden abilities
choices.visible_reward: Obtain key information to determine if the other party is friend or foe
choices.risk_hint: May fall into the other party's verbal traps

text.content:
Chen Ji stared directly into Ji Wujiu's eyes, unflinching: "Since Your Excellency knows all the truths about the Tianji Record, surely you also understand—every generation of keeper has been devoured by Heavenly Dao's will. May I ask—is Your Excellency here to harvest for Heavenly Dao, or..."

He paused微微, his words sharp as a blade: "Or does Your Excellency wish to use this chess piece of mine to... challenge the true Chess Player?"

dialogue.content:
Ji Wujiu's eyes flashed with an unusual gleam, then he burst into laughter.

"Good! Excellent! Chen Ji! No wonder you, a废物, could survive the machinations of three major sects—"

His laughter abruptly stopped, his expression suddenly cold and stern: "You speak correctly. Heavenly Dao's Eye is the true Chess Player of this game, and this envoy... wants to overturn the entire chessboard."

choices.description: Retreat to advance—表面上顺从，实则暗中收集情报，寻找对方破绽
choices.visible_reward: Obtain more information without exposing your hand
choices.risk_hint: The other party may see through your intentions

text.content:
Chen Ji bowed again, his posture even more humble: "Your Excellency's words strike like thunder, this fool is confused, I humbly request Your Excellency to enlighten me—what does Your Excellency wish this chess piece to do?"

He lowered his head, yet the corners of his lips curled into an almost imperceptible arc.

废物 should act like废物. Since the other party needs this chess piece, they will inevitably reveal more cards. And what he needed to do was simply wait patiently.

dialogue.content:
Ji Wujiu glanced at him deeply: "You are quite composed."

He stopped beating around the bush, speaking directly: "This envoy knows what you're thinking—you simply want to fish for information. Very well, this envoy will give you a proposition you cannot refuse today."

Golden light blazed in his palm, and a jade slip emanating forbidden aura materialized from thin air.

"This is the 'Heavenly Fate Deconstruction', which can help you break free from the Tianji Record's shackles—elevating you from a chess piece to a true Chess Player."

choices.description: Do not trust any information lightly; secretly activate the Tianji Record for brief foresight to assess the greatest threat
choices.visible_reward: Obtain crucial foresight for the next three hours
choices.risk_hint: The consumption of Heavenly Fate is irreversible, and may be detected by Ji Wuqiu

text.content:
Chen Ji lowered his gaze, his fingertips quietly reaching into his sleeve, gently stroking the Tianji Record fragment.

Foreseeing the next three hours cost five points of Heavenly Fate—this was already one of his few remaining reserves. But facing this unfathomable Ji Wuqiu, he had to know whether the other was friend or foe.

The fragment was slightly cool as the Heavenly Secrets flowed.

In an instant, countless fragmented images flooded into his Mental Sea—within three hours, this place would turn to ruins, and he himself... would be drawn into a storm far beyond imagination.

dialogue.content:
Just as the prophetic vision flashed by, Ji Wuqiu's gaze slightly narrowed.

"Interesting."

He looked at Chen Ji with an enigmatic smile: "The aura of the Tianji Record... indeed cannot be hidden from this envoy. But it's fine, this envoy is not your enemy. On the contrary—"

He raised his hand, and the scroll of forbidden jade hung between the two of them.

"What this envoy brings is your only chance to escape."

text.content:
Chen Ji stood in place, his gaze fixed on that scroll of forbidden jade, his expression dark and uncertain.

An opportunity to break free from the Tianji Record's shackles...

The temptation was too great. Great enough to make him forget the vigilance from moments ago, forget the various doubts in Ji Wuqiu's words, forget—Master Mo's warning that was never explained.

But it was precisely this temptation that made him even more alert.

There is never a free lunch in this world, especially when the meal smells intoxicating enough to suffocate.

dialogue.content:
"You're doubting this envoy."

Ji Wuqiu showed no anger; instead, he displayed approval: "That's good. If the Tianji Record's bearer were truly a fool, this envoy would be disappointed instead."

He took a step forward, his oppressive aura suddenly收敛, replaced by an almost sincere tone:

"Chen Ji, you should understand—the Heavenly Eye has never regarded you as a chess piece; it only sees you as... fuel. Every time you use the Tianji Record, your Heavenly Fate Value is draining, and when that value reaches zero—"

He paused meaningfully: "You will become the next sacrifice devoured by Heaven."

text.content:
Chen Ji's fingertips trembled slightly.

Heavenly Fate Value reaching zero... sacrifice...

He thought of those vague records within the Tianji Record, of the inexplicable disappearances of past bearers, of the occasional look of compassion that Master Mo occasionally showed—that gaze, like looking at someone already marked for death.

Could it be that his chess game was destined to be a dead-end from the start?

No.

Chen Ji took a deep breath, pressing all emotions into the depths of his Mental Sea. No matter the truth, he would never easily trust anyone—including this envoy of unknown origins from the imperial dynasty.

choice.prompt: Ji Wuqiu's temptation and threat intertwined, forcing Chen Ji to make a choice amid limited information—

choices.description: Directly ask Ji Wuqiu what he wants Chen Ji to do, weigh the pros and cons before deciding
choices.visible_reward: Clarify the terms of the transaction and potential risks
choices.risk_hint: The other party may use information advantage to further apply pressure

text.content:
Chen Ji raised his eyes,直视 Ji Wuqiu's two eyes: "There is no free lunch in the world. Your Excellency is so generous; what you seek must be no small matter."

His voice was calm, yet carried an undeniable edge: "The junior wishes to know, what exactly do you want me to do?"

dialogue.content:
Ji Wuqiu clapped his hands and laughed: "Direct!"

His gaze turned sharp: "The only thing this envoy wants you to do is—the Heavenly Eye will descend celestial punishment in three months.届时 you will need to use the Tianji Record as a medium to disrupt its foresight."

"In simple terms..."

A grim, cold smile curved at the corner of his mouth: "This envoy wants you to buy this envoy three breaths of time."

choices.description: Agree to cooperate for now, secretly leave a backdoor, seek opportunities to escape or counter
choices.visible_cost: Need to continue acting, may reveal flaws
choices.visible_reward: Buy time to lay out plans while obtaining more intelligence
choices.risk_hint: If exposed, it will completely enrage Ji Wuqiu

text.content:
Chen Ji pondered for a moment, then finally slowly nodded: "Since Your Excellency intends this, Chen Ji... is willing to hear the details."

His tone carried appropriate hesitation and deliberation, neither appearing too eager nor excessively resistant.

A废物 should have废物's appearance—timid, indecisive, yet unable to resist temptation. This was the Chen Ji Ji Wuqiu wanted to see.

As for the real him... that would wait until Ji Wuqiu revealed all his cards.

dialogue.content:
Ji Wuqiu nodded in satisfaction, pushing the jade scroll forward an inch: "Good. Take this first. The secret technique recorded within can temporarily suppress the Tianji Record's erosion. As for the specific action—"

He changed the subject: "After you complete the first phase of the task, this envoy will inform you."

He turned to leave, but paused mid-air, nonchalantly tossing out a sentence without turning his head:

"By the way, Su Qingyao... is a good girl. If you wish to protect her safety, you'd better grow stronger quickly."

As the words fell, his oppressive aura receded like a tide, and Ji Wuqiu's figure vanished beyond the hall's doors.

choices.description: Do not trust any words from Ji Wujiu, refuse the deal, and maintain independence
choices.visible_cost: May lose important opportunities and offend the imperial dynasty forces
choices.visible_reward: Maintain autonomy,不被任何势力裹挟
choices.risk_hint: Ji Wujiu may turn hostile on the spot

text.content:
Chen Ji suddenly smiled.

The smile was faint, yet carried a chilling malevolence that made one's heart tremble. He no longer bowed but stood with hands clasped behind his back, meeting Ji Wujiu's gaze as an equal.

"Many thanks for the honored envoy's kindness. However—"

He spoke each word with deliberate weight: "Chen某's life belongs to Chen Ji himself to wager. Your chessboard, Chen Ji refuses to play."

dialogue.content:
A deathly silence filled the great hall.

Ji Wujiu slowly turned, his gaze like a blade cutting across Chen Ji's face. That terrifying pressure descended once more, heavier and more oppressive than before, as if intending to crush Chen Ji's very soul into dust.

Yet Chen Ji remained utterly motionless.

"Courageous."

Ji Wujiu's voice was cold as millennium-old glacial ice: "But this envoy advises you—one who refuses to pick a side in this chess game... often dies the fastest."

text.content:
Fragrant incense curled through the hall, yet could not dispel the stagnant air.

Chen Ji stood in place. Ji Wujiu had departed long ago, but he could still feel that faint yet persistent scrutiny—as if an invisible pair of eyes gazed down upon him from impossibly high and distant realms.

Heavenly Dao's Eye.

He remembered now. In that fragmentary premonition, he had once glimpsed an eye. Its pupil was pure silver-white, devoid of any emotion, containing only the most frigid scrutiny to the extreme.

Was that the Heavenly Dao itself?

Chen Ji lowered his gaze to his own palm.

The Tianji Record Fragment hidden in his sleeve remained faintly warm, the lingering resonance of the Heavenly Dao Origin Summoning Token. He closed his eyes, letting that warmth spread through his entire body.

Ji Wujiu's words still echoed in his ears—

"Every time you use the Tianji Record, your Heavenly Fate Value drains away, and when that value reaches zero—you will become the next sacrifice devoured by the Heavenly Dao."

Sacrifice...

He suddenly felt like laughing.

He had orchestrated the world, left nothing to chance, prided himself on manipulating all beings between his fingers—and in the end, he himself was the greatest joke of all.

Yet Chen Ji ultimately did not laugh aloud.

Because he recalled something—a phrase Mo Xiansheng had once told him.

"Within the chess game, if a piece wishes to turn the tables, it must transform itself into part of the chessboard."

At the time, he thought it was merely obscure gibberish, but now upon careful contemplation, it revealed an entirely different flavor.

Ji Wujiu wished to overturn the chessboard. The Heavenly Dao's Eye sought to bring all under control. And he—

What he must do was perhaps neither becoming a chess piece nor overturning the board.

But to carve out a realm of his own from within the seams of the chessboard.

The残阳 finally sank behind the mountains, and darkness claimed the hall.

Chen Ji slowly opened his eyes, his gaze falling upon the spot where Ji Wujiu had stood—a trace of barely perceptible Spiritual Light remained there.

He approached and bent down to examine it.

It was an extremely delicate jade talisman, translucent throughout, bearing an ancient and simple character "Yu" inscribed upon it. Had his eyesight not been exceptionally sharp, he would never have discovered this object's existence.

Left deliberately by Ji Wujiu? Or... an oversight?

Chen Ji tucked the jade talisman into his sleeve, a thoughtful gleam flickering in his eyes.

Regardless of which possibility, this jade talisman warranted careful study. And that transaction concerning "Heavenly Fate Deconstruction"...

His lips curved slightly, revealing a meaningful smile.

No rush. The chess game has only just begun.

Just then, soft footsteps sounded from outside the hall.

"Chen Ji?"

It was Su Qingyao's voice, carrying traces of inquiry and wariness.

Chen Ji immediately composed his expression, reverting to that servile Servant Disciple. He strode quickly toward the hall entrance, his posture impeccably deferential: "Senior Sister Su, why have you come?"

Su Qingyao's gaze lingered on his face for a moment, seemingly trying to discern something from his eyes, yet only seeing a expanse of timid weakness.

"That aura just now..." she frowned. "Who was it?"

Chen Ji kept his head bowed, his voice trembling slightly: "Replying to Senior Sister, it was... was an envoy from the imperial dynasty. It has nothing to do with your disciple—he merely passed through the Tianqing Sect and delivered some instruction."

He paused, as if gathering courage, then raised his head: "Senior Sister, your disciple... your disciple is so frightened..."

Su Qingyao gazed at this cowering youth before her, her heart filled with mixed emotions.

That oppressive aura just now—even through layers of halls and chambers, she could perceive it clearly—an existence that transcended all her previous understanding. And yet this youth, dismissed as worthless, had somehow survived under such pressure?

No.

She refused to believe he was worthless. Never had she believed it.

Yet she had investigated countless times and found no evidence. Every time he flawlessly portrayed that timid Servant Disciple, as if that懦弱的 facade were his true face.

"...Go rest for now."

She finally spoke, her voice carrying a thread of weariness: "The sect will handle matters concerning the imperial dynasty."

Chen Ji seemed overjoyed, nodding repeatedly before retreating with bows.

Only when his figure vanished into the night did Su Qingyao slowly withdraw her gaze, murmuring to herself: "Chen Ji... just how many secrets are you still hiding?"

Night wind brushed past the Tianqing Sect's Mountain Gate, scattering the final wisps of残阳.

Chen Ji walked alone along the path back to the Servants' Quarters, his steps neither hurried nor slow. He raised his head toward the night sky—countless stars dotted the heavens, the Milky Way stretched across, as if unchanged since antiquity.

Yet he knew this world was far from as peaceful as it appeared.

The Heavenly Dao's Eye loomed on high, holding the fates of all beings in its grasp; the imperial envoy harbored hidden ambitions, plotting to overturn the chessboard; the Three Great Sects engaged in covert struggles while demonic path forces prowled with predatory intent. And he—a wretch who should have died long ago—struggled to find his own path of survival within this intricate chess game.

He halted his steps, withdrawing that delicate jade talisman from his sleeve.

Beneath the moonlight, the "Yu" character faintly gleamed with an eerie luminescence, as if silently revealing some ancient secret.

Ji Wujiu... Heavenly Dao's Eye... Cang Yutian... Chess Players...

These names swirled in his mind, gradually weaving into a vast net. And he stood at the net's center, enemies on all sides.

Chen Ji tucked the jade talisman into his chest, a cold smile curling at his lips.

So what if enemies surround me on all sides?

This life of mine has always been one of carving a bloody path through desperate circumstances.

The night deepened. In a corner of the Tianqing Sect, a solitary lamp flickered to life in Chen Ji's room. He spread out paper, lifted his brush, and began to write—his unique method of documentation, recording everything he witnessed and heard that day, sparing no detail.

Upon the page, the ink still glistening: "Ji Wujiu, Yutian Pavilion Emissary, descendant of Cang Yutian. His purpose is to interfere with the Heavenly Dao's Eye's heavenly punishment—time: three months from now."

At the final line, his brush tip hesitated微微.

Then he added a note: "Remark: This person mentioned Su Qingyao, intending to test boundaries. This person... cannot be trusted."
